searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase two — improved brainstorm after gevurah the awtsmoos conceals and reveals, so a boundless dream can enter form; awtsmoos.com needs a movie covenant small enough to test, yet wide enough to survive the storm. revised center of gravity the project should not attempt to “merge four apps.” it should establish three shared contracts and make each app choose how much of them it consumes: 1. movie contract — declarative document, validation, time, capabilities, feature inventory. 2. asset intent contract — movie nodes request existing procedural generators through stable descriptors. 3. ui recipe contract — declarative mobile first studio shell and reusable app ui pieces. everything else is adapter territory. movie contract minimum viable completeness the first implementation should support enough vocabulary to build the required proof movie without pretending to cover infinite cinema on day one: movie metadata and exact duration; scenes with explicit duration/order; layers with start/end windows; transforms and opacity; reusable assets/actors; 2d shapes and text; chart/tutorial primitives; 3d primitive/procedural asset references; particles; camera cues; keyframes and easing; transitions; captions/audio cue metadata; groups; validation and feature inventory. extensibility comes from a typed node registry/capability catalog instead of adding speculative dozens of fields. runtime model the compiler should create a small immutable ish execution artifact: normalized document; ordered scene spans; asset lookup map; actor lookup map; capability requirements; warnings/errors; total duration; helper for frameat(time) or resolve(time). a resolved frame need not contain raster pixels. it contains the semantic scene state at time t, including active layers and interpolated values. render adapters turn that state into pixels. 2d realization strategy prefer canvas 2d for the first shared renderer because it is browser native and ideal for text, shapes, diagrams, charts, callouts, and particles. keep a renderer registry so svg/dom can be added later. the canvas adapter can remain generic if it only knows canonical layer types and simple drawing operations. procedural character/complex image layers can supply a bitmap/canvas source through asset adapters. 3d realization strategy do not write a new three.js engine. build a thin adapter that can map canonical movie cues into whichever shared three/procedural runtime is already public. where existing core provides asset generators but not a full browser three scene host, the flagship can bind an app/runtime adapter rather than infecting core contracts with global three assumptions. character strategy canonical actors are identity records. a scene layer refers to actorid and animation/action cues. the adapter resolves the actor through existing procedural human/rig systems. this allows one character identity to recur across scenes and camera angles. infographic/tutorial strategy create first class semantic primitives rather than making ai hand author hundreds of low level rectangles: callout arrow chart progress stepcard highlightbox codepanel comparison adapters may expand these into shapes/text. this keeps ai output compact and repairable. particle strategy canonical particle layers should accept named presets plus deterministic seed and a bounded property bag. the adapter can map to the existing procedural particle engine when compatible or use a simple canvas fallback for 2d only apps. ui strategy the shared ui grammar should focus on reducing studio boilerplate, not replacing every component system. initial node types: element text button/action list/repeater input/field conditional slot/custom mount studio helpers then describe higher level composition: toolbar preview surface navigator tabs sheet/panel timeline container inspector container status/export area this hierarchy keeps the low level renderer generic while studio recipes remain expressive. security and ai safety whitelist tags/attributes; no inline scripts; no raw event source strings; action names resolve through registry; text is text by default; url policies for media sources; movie nodes validated before adapters receive them; capability discovery lets ai choose valid alternatives. integration strategy by app animator: expose canonical import/export and use its strong character/camera/procedural systems as adapters. avoid rewriting deep animator internals unless a parallel agent already provides a stable bridge. nesher studio: expose canonical project/movie conversion and export provider. reuse nle/export rather than moving it wholesale into core. video editor: support canonical simple clips/scenes/captions and preserve compact timeline ux. mitzvah studio: support canonical visual object conversion and shared ui recipes where easy, preserving inspector/outliner workflow. awtsmoos studio: consume all shared contracts directly and become the integration proof. proof movie design twelve scenes at fifteen seconds each is structurally simple and exactly 180 seconds. not every scene must have the same pacing internally; each can contain multiple beats/keyframes. possible scene arc: 1. creation burst — particles + title + cosmic 3d reveal. 2. world emergence — procedural terrain/city, crane/wide camera. 3. character arrival — two reusable people, medium/low angle shots. 4. tutorial board — 2d steps, arrows, kinetic labels. 5. data story — animated bars/line/progress and callouts. 6. split dimensions — 2d overlays over 3d object/environment. 7. dialogue/performance — close up/over shoulder character shots. 8. procedural build — architecture/shape assembly with annotations. 9. motion lesson — paths, easing comparison, particles/trails. 10. climax — orbit camera, particle field, layered text, environment motion. 11. recap — cards, chart summary, character callback. 12. credits/revelation — calm camera, typography, particles, fade. verification strategy refined unit tests prove pure contracts. browser tests prove adapters/ui. the proof movie doubles as an integration fixture. export is validated by artifact existence, non zero size, duration metadata if inspectable, and representative visual frames where practical. phase two conclusion: one pure semantic core, thin render/export adapters, narrow secure ui grammar, and a flagship app that proves the whole chain end to end.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase two — specific execution plan the awtsmoos turns possibility into ordered deed, one vessel at a time; awtsmoos.com will gain shared cinematic truth without erasing each studio's rhyme. stage 1 — refresh reality after concurrent writes 1. re scan git status short for movie/core/ui/studio paths. 2. search for files created in the last planning interval containing movie capability, feature catalog, studio unification, ui recipe, scene compiler, or timeline contracts. 3. read the public exports/package files for awtsmoos procedural core. 4. read the newly landed capability/movie files, if any, in full. 5. search libs/awtsmoos and adjacent shared libraries for a general json dom/ui renderer. 6. confirm whether apps/awtsmoos studio remains absent. 7. record exact observed paths in the evidence ledger before code. stage 2 — choose canonical implementation home decision order: if a valid canonical movie namespace has landed in procedural core, extend it. else if a shared movie namespace has landed elsewhere with real consumers, preserve it and add compatibility exports only if architecture justifies it. else create a new core/movie/ namespace inside procedural core. for ui: if a general shared ui recipe/renderer already exists, improve it in its existing home. else create libs/awtsmoos ui with only the strict json recipe → dom/action/state features required by studio apps. stage 3 — shared movie contract implementation required pure capabilities: document normalization; validation with json paths and repair hints; capability catalog; deterministic scene timeline; global to local time resolution; interpolation/easing; feature inventory; asset intent normalization; compiler facade. required semantic node families: shapes and text; tutorial/infographic primitives; actors/people; procedural/imported 3d assets; particles; cameras/lights; captions/audio cues; groups and transitions. no browser globals in pure contract files. stage 4 — procedural asset bridge read actual existing generator registries, then expose a movie facing bridge that: resolves generator + recipe descriptors; preserves deterministic seed; reports unsupported generators clearly; returns portable generation result metadata where possible; never duplicates mature geometry/character/particle generation. only genuinely reusable app local generators discovered during inspection may be moved into core, and only after tracing all current importers. stage 5 — shared ui contract implement a narrow secure grammar: normalized recipe node; safe tag/attribute policy; dom creation; named action registry; state value binding; conditional/repeater support; custom mount slots; studio shell recipe helpers; mobile first responsive tokens/helpers. avoid raw html/event source execution. stage 6 — flagship awtsmoos studio create the new app if still absent: tiny html shell; tiny boot module; session state; movie loader/compiler; playback/seek clock; preview host selecting 2d/3d adapters; ai json/spec editing/import path; shared ui recipe + actions; export provider interface; mobile first layout; example movie loader. the app should demonstrate shared systems directly rather than copying components from the other apps. stage 7 — proof movie create 12 scene modules, each 15 seconds, for exactly 180 seconds. each scene must deliberately exercise different features, with reusable actor/asset ids across scenes. the manifest compiler must assert exact duration before playback. stage 8 — existing app integration for each app, first inspect whether another agent has already integrated the shared movie contract. if not: create a small adapter in the app; wire it through the real app entry/import graph via a full file hash guarded rewrite only when necessary; preserve app specific data models and workflows; prove import/export or canonical playback in runtime. do not perform cosmetic rewrites unrelated to integration. stage 9 — first source pass completion gate no tests begin until the first planned source implementation is complete, per project coding instructions. before testing, ensure all planned source modules exist, no obvious todo placeholder stands in for behavior, and all source files remain small/readable. stage 10 — verification syntax checks; focused node unit tests; existing app/core tests; local server/browser route checks; console review; desktop layout; mobile layout; representative movie seeks; ai invalid→repairable validation test; feature inventory assertion; exact 180 second assertion; export attempt through real provider; inspect encoded artifact if produced. stage 11 — readback and delta read every touched file in full. write a new post write delta file, never overwriting these planning files. compare: what phase one imagined; what phase two constrained; what source actually contains; what verification proves; what remains. if required items remain, complete a second full file writing pass and re verify. source write laws full file writes only. tabs for indentation. no minified functions. split modules before they exceed the project file size rule. b"h / boruch hashem / blessed is he header in compatible source files. detailed poetic jsdoc about the awtsmoos and awtsmoos.com. re read before overwrite; use hashes for contested files. never reset/stash/delete other agents' work. this plan is specific about behavior, but intentionally defers exact legacy filenames until the mandatory live refresh prevents stale plan collisions.
